title: Row With Maximum Ones
summary: Given a m x n binary matrix, identify the row with the highest number of ones.
statement: Given a m x n binary matrix, identify the row with the highest number of ones. If multiple rows have the same highest count, choose the row with the smallest index. Return an array with the row index and the count of ones.
constraints: mat is a nonempty binary matrix.
Find the row containing the most ones.
Return [row_index,ones_count], choosing the smallest index on a tie.
hints: Keep the best index and count seen so far.
Update only for a strictly larger count so an earlier tied row remains selected.
Each row is evaluated once, and the invariant retains the required maximum with smallest-index tie-breaking.
editorial: Each row is evaluated once, and the invariant retains the required maximum with smallest-index tie-breaking.

tests.explanation: Both rows contain one one, so the smaller index zero wins.
Row one contains two ones and is uniquely best.
